plan.title: bug(hooks,scope): write fence has no per-worktree story binding, so in-session sub-agents cannot run a multi-story cohort on Claude Code

narratives.Description: The PreToolUse write fence learns which story a write belongs to only from a spawn-time bound path or from DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE in the hook process environment. Workers that share one hook environment cannot each carry their own pin, so a worker worktree that holds more than one active brief is refused every product write as multiple-eligible. This story makes the fence read the story for a dispatch-registered linked worktree from its worker-auth assignment record, with closed refusal rules, and leaves unregistered linked worktrees and the main worktree unchanged.
narratives.Overview:
1. Write fence, no spawn bound path, linked worktree: read the worker-auth assignment for the write's worktree through the validated reader. When it returns an assignment, resolve the story by a unique `story_id` match against eligible active briefs. Assignment only. No branch tokens. The check-time `untied` outcome never admits a write.
2. Linked worktree: refuse when the reader fails for any reason (corrupt index, orphan, duplicate, malformed or missing registered record), because membership is then unknowable or broken. Also refuse when the assigned story is missing, ineligible or ambiguous, when an environment pin names a different story, and when a spawn bound path names a different story. No fall-through to branch or single-eligible selection. The refusal names the failure kind and one repair step.
3. Linked worktree with a validated clean absence (the reader succeeds and reports no assignment for this worktree): today's behaviour, unchanged. The main worktree never consults the registry.
4. The matcher derives `story_id` the same way launch does, or launch refuses a brief with no `plan.id`.
5. Stated guarantee: destination-scoped cooperative fencing. The trusted writer is dispatch PREP. It is not worker isolation. Coverage is Write/Edit, plus recognized shell destination forms when that policy is set to enforce. Other shell writes are not covered.
6. Claude adapter text names the in-session sequence: the parent launches through `swarm:launch` so each worker worktree is registered; the parent starts the session ritual in each worker worktree; the parent holds no environment pin; each sub-agent is given its worktree's absolute path. One headless process per story is the named fallback until item 7 passes.
7. Acceptance: a live two-story run through `swarm:launch` on Claude Code, in nested `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<sid>` destinations, with no environment pin. Each worker makes an admitted in-scope product write and is refused out of scope. The same run records whether the launch-minted lease admits the session's sub-agents. Before the change the same run is refused as multiple-eligible. A product-file write and a lifecycle-brief edit are tested separately. A corrupt-index case is tested for a registered worktree, an unregistered linked worktree and the main worktree.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator running several stories at once, I want the write fence to take the story of a worker worktree from the assignment record that dispatch wrote for it, so that workers that share one hook environment can each write inside their own story without a session-wide pin.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Move the story-id derivation that swarm launch uses into worker-auth-assignment.ts (exported), and call it from launch.ts so the record and the matcher share one derivation.
2. In scope.ts add one resolver for the write fence: given a linked worktree root, call readWorkerAuthAssignment; map reader failure to refuse, clean absence to no-binding, and an assignment to a unique story_id match against eligible active briefs (missing, ineligible or ambiguous refuses). No branch tokens. No untied outcome.
3. In dispatcher.ts, on the direct-write path for a linked worktree effectiveRoot, call the resolver before inspectActiveScope. A resolved story becomes the bound path. An environment pin or spawn bound path that names a different story refuses. Refusals name the failure kind and one repair step. The main worktree does not call the reader.
4. Tests: unit tests for the resolver in scope.test.ts; dispatcher fixtures with a real temporary repository and two linked worktrees under .deft-scratch/worktrees/ in dispatcher-active-scope.test.ts and dispatcher-effective-root.test.ts; derivation tests in worker-auth-assignment.test.ts and launch.test.ts.
5. Rewrite host-claude-code.md Step 2g item 3 as the four-step in-session sequence with the headless per-story fallback, and state the guarantee and its limits there.
6. Add a CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry.

## In plain English

Problem: the write hook must know which story a write belongs to. It reads that from a spawn-time path or from one process environment variable. Claude Code sub-agents share the parent's environment, so a cohort of several stories cannot run as in-session sub-agents there. The issue proposes that the hook read the story from a per-worktree record that dispatch already writes.

This arc asks three independent critics whether that problem statement holds at the pinned code, and whether the proposed direction is safe and sufficient. It does not ingest, and it does not start implementation.

## Pains

| Id | Pain |
| --- | --- |
| `P1` | On Claude Code, a multi-story cohort cannot run as in-session sub-agents: with more than one fencing active brief the write fence needs a pin, and the only pin sources are a spawn-time bound path and one session-wide environment variable. |
| `P2` | The Claude Code swarm adapter text tells the parent to set each worker's worktree path, but names no mechanism, so the documented implement path and the working path (one headless process per story) differ. |

## In plain English

The missing worktree binding is real in the pinned code. Reading the existing assignment record is a reasonable direction, but it does not yet establish a working Claude Code cohort path or isolate one worker from another. The design needs an explicit authority boundary, refusal behavior, and a demonstrated launch-to-write path before it can claim to resolve the reported problem.

1. **blocks-the-design — Target-worktree binding is not worker-to-story binding.**

   **Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:1220–1282` selects `effectiveRoot` from mutation targets and accepts linked worktrees sharing the repository’s Git common directory. `host-session-identity.ts` identifies Claude actors by `session_id`, not `agent_id`. `worker-auth-assignment.ts:645–724` validates the destination record and index, but does not compare its `dispatch_id` with the calling worker.

   **Failure mode:** Worker A can name a file in worker B’s worktree. With a shared session identity and no environment pin, the proposed lookup selects B’s assignment and B’s fence. It answers “which story governs this destination?” without proving “is this worker assigned to that story?” This requires neither a branch rename nor registry tampering.

   **Disposition:** Before binding, explicitly choose the guarantee. Destination-scoped cooperative fencing is defensible, but must not be presented as worker isolation or as satisfying an unverified #5894 binding contract. If worker isolation is required, a caller-to-assignment check is missing. Resolve that dependency rather than leaving it simultaneously required and out of scope.

2. **blocks-the-design — The assignment resolver needs closed failure semantics, not just a successful lookup.**

   **Evidence:** `readWorkerAuthAssignment` already distinguishes clean absence from corrupt indexes, orphan records, duplicate registrations, missing registered records, and malformed assignments. `scope.ts:415–460` currently permits an unmatched environment pin to fall back to the sole eligible brief. Its branch resolver checks branch tokens before consulting worker-auth.

   **Failure mode:** Treating registry errors as absence, or applying the existing single-eligible fallback after an assignment conflict, could admit a different story when the assigned story has disappeared or become ineligible. Reusing `bindBranchToActiveStory` wholesale would also retain branch-first authority.

   **Disposition:** Require the existing validated assignment reader, unique `story_id` matching against eligible active briefs, and explicit refusal for corrupt records, missing/ineligible assigned stories, and conflicting environment pins. Those failures must not fall through to branch or single-candidate selection. Clean absence can retain current behavior. Define how explicit spawn binding interacts with this rule without comparing a child destination’s story against an unrelated parent-root assignment.

3. **blocks-the-design — A later-write fix does not establish the in-session launch path.**

   **Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:2536–2543` derives spawn binding from `spawnConsult.destPath`, then inspects scope at `effectiveRoot`. The Claude adapter’s Step 2g requires an isolated worktree path but supplies no concrete transport for it. `dest-place.ts` documents a Grok `tool_input.cwd` path and explicitly says destination preparation itself does not mint reservations or child occupancy.

   **Failure mode:** A valid worker assignment can resolve subsequent file writes while implementation spawn still fails at the parent root, or the child starts without the required destination preparation and admission. The proposed four outcomes therefore do not yet demonstrate relief of the Claude cohort pain.

   **Disposition:** Require a concrete supported launch sequence and a two-story acceptance scenario covering spawn, destination preparation, occupancy/ritual admission, and subsequent product-file writes without a shared story pin. Alternatively, narrow this change to destination scope resolution and retain the in-session cohort problem as unresolved. Do not claim the headless workaround is verified by this critique.

4. **sharpens-framing — The evaluator reproduction proves ambiguity, not universal live-hook refusal.**

   **Evidence:** `scope.ts:134–139` and `inspectActiveScope` confirm the two pin sources and multiple-candidate refusal. However, `dispatcher.ts:2555–2565` preserves the outside-payload-root carve-out when scope is not ready. Its earlier lifecycle exemptions cover proposed and completed briefs; those excerpts do not establish a blanket active-brief exemption.

   **Failure mode:** A reproduction using external sibling worktrees can allow writes despite evaluator ambiguity, while the usual nested `.deft-scratch/worktrees/` layout denies them. Calling the cohort categorically impossible hides this layout-dependent behavior and leaves the earlier four successful Edits unexplained.

   **Disposition:** State the confirmed defect as missing assignment-based resolution on the gated write path. Include nested and external worktree layouts in the verification matrix, and distinguish product writes from lifecycle-brief edits. The existing carve-out is a plausible explanation, not a verified reconstruction of #6185.

5. **sharpens-framing — Shell coverage must remain an explicit limitation.**

   **Evidence:** `dispatcher.ts:1295–1328` states that shell destination-form enforcement defaults to off. When enabled, coverage is limited to recognized forms such as `git restore`, `git checkout --`, and `rm/rmdir`; unresolved shell targets remain outside this deny.

   **Failure mode:** A successful Write/Edit demonstration could be reported as covering worker writes generally, while shell mutations do not consult the new binding.

   **Disposition:** Specify coverage by tool surface and policy mode. Exercise recognized shell forms with enforcement enabled, and do not claim arbitrary shell-write isolation. Expanding shell parsing is not necessary to fix assignment lookup.

I favor reusing the validated assignment reader over branch-name inference: it already provides destination canonicalization and registry-consistency checks. Branch inference has the advantage of requiring no new record, but its branch-first behavior does not meet this proposal’s stated resistance to branch-name sidesteps.

**Verification:** I used read-only `git show` and `git grep` at dispatch SHA `82a53abab79e5c513b3a4c582075db70205a301b` for scope resolution, dispatcher root admission and exemptions, host identity, worker-auth assignment reading, destination preparation, and the Claude adapter. `git diff cd76d7d75 82a53abab --` showed no changes to `scope.ts` or `dispatcher.ts`; `git ls-tree` confirmed the four named active briefs at the earlier SHA.

I did not execute the evaluator reproduction, tests, or a live Claude hook/Agent session. The host’s actual tool schema, environment behavior, occupancy behavior across concurrent children, and the full #5894 contract remain unverified. I read only the supplied thread snapshot through comment `6838150346`; no network access, file edits, or agent dispatch occurred.

## In plain English

The core problem is real. When more than one story brief is active, the write hook can only learn which story a write belongs to from a spawn-time path or from one environment variable. Claude Code sub-agents share the parent's environment, so they cannot each carry a different story. Reading the story from the per-worktree record that `swarm:launch` already writes is a sound direction, and it fits the existing code well. The record is keyed by worktree root, and the hook already works out the worktree root of every Write/Edit target.

The issue still needs four corrections before it can bind:

- **The Grok contrast does not hold in the code.** The Grok spawn-time pin only exists when the destination has exactly one active brief. That is not the multi-brief cohort case the issue describes, so the problem is probably not specific to Claude.
- **The record only exists for worktrees made by `swarm:launch`.** That command writes the record only when it is given the GitHub-auth flags. Worktrees that Claude creates itself have no record, so the fix does nothing for them unless the dispatch path is stated.
- **Reuse the assignment matcher, not the whole check-time binder.** Reusing `bindBranchToActiveStory` as-is would let the branch name decide first, which is the #5894 sidestep. It would also bring in an "untied" outcome that must never admit a write.
- **Story ids can disagree.** When a brief has no `plan.id`, launch records a filename-based `story_id`, but the matcher only compares against `plan.id`.

None of these needs a new mechanism. Each one changes how the lean must be stated or scoped.

## Findings

### F1 — sharpens-framing: the "works on Grok Build" contrast is not supported by the code; the problem is likely not host-specific

Evidence:
- `git show 82a53abab:packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, around L2537–2543: `spawnBoundPath` is computed only when `isSpawnTool(toolName)` is true. A child's later Write/Edit is not a spawn tool, so it falls back to `env`.
- Same file, `uniqueActiveBasenameFromDestPath` (around L2841–2856): it returns a pin only when the destination's `xbrief/active` + `vbrief/active` hold exactly one artifact name.
- The issue's own "Worktree alone" paragraph, citing #4714, says each worker branch carries every cohort brief in `xbrief/active/`. In that case the Grok spawn-time `boundPath` is `null`, and the Grok spawn itself goes through the unpinned `multiple-eligible` path.

Failure mode: the lean is scoped and tested as a Claude-only gap, and item 4 claims a Grok benefit ("stops depending on the spawn-time pin surviving") for a dependency the code does not have. Grok multi-brief cohorts stay untested. The headline was already withdrawn once on #6185 as not reproduced, and its four allowed Edits are still unexplained. Without an end-to-end repro, the fix may target a path that is not firing where people think it is.

Disposition consequence: state P1 host-neutrally: any cohort whose workers share a hook environment, or whose destination holds more than one active brief. Replace item 4 with a statement of what Grok actually does today. Require an end-to-end hook repro before and after the fix, run in a `.deft-scratch/worktrees/<sid>` destination (which is under the payload root, so the #2885 outside-root carve-out does not apply), on Claude Code and on Grok.

### F2 — sharpens-framing: the binding record exists only for `swarm:launch`-created worktrees; the lean must name that as the Claude dispatch path (this also answers Q3 and P2)

Evidence:

## Summary

The PreToolUse write fence learns which story a write belongs to from two sources only: a spawn-time `boundPath`, or `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` in the hook process environment. With more than one fencing active brief and no pin, it fails closed as `multiple-eligible` (#4007).

On Claude Code, in-session sub-agents (`Agent`) run inside the parent process and share its environment. One environment means one pin for the whole cohort. So a multi-story cohort cannot run as in-session sub-agents on Claude Code. It works on Grok Build, where `spawn_subagent` takes a `cwd` and the pin is bound at spawn.

The runtime already holds a per-worktree story record (the worker-auth assignment, #3663, and `bindBranchToActiveStory`, #5855). The write fence does not read it.

## Evidence

Evaluator-level reproduction at `cd76d7d75` (v0.129.7), on a delivery-branch checkout with four active briefs (#5710, #5882, #6203, #6212):

- `inspectActiveScope(root, { env })` with no `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE`: `ready=false`, `denyKind=multiple-eligible`, message names all four briefs.
- Same call with `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` set to one brief's basename: `ready=true`, bound to that brief.

Run with `tsx` against `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts`. This is the evaluator, not a live hook run. I did not run an end-to-end Edit through the hook in a worker worktree.

Code at that SHA:

- `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` `pinFrom`: `boundPath`, else `env[DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE]`.
- `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` (about L2537): `boundPath` is set only when the tool is a spawn tool. Later direct writes by the child fall back to the environment.
- `packages/core/src/hooks/classify/host-session-identity.ts`: Claude Code identity is the payload `session_id`; `agent_id` is not the owner key. Parent and sub-agents are one actor.
- `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` `bindBranchToActiveStory` and `admitUntiedWithWorkerAuth`: bind by branch token, then by the worker-auth assignment `story_id`. Called from `resolveSoftMissingAcTargets` (check / pre-PR), not from `inspectActiveScope`.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-claude-code.md` Step 2g item 3 says "the worktree path set to the agent's isolated git worktree". It names no mechanism, and `packages/core/src/swarm/dest-place.ts` has no Claude path. The Claude `Agent` tool has no `cwd` field.

## Why the listed recoveries do not work on this host

- **Environment pin.** One value for every sub-agent. A parent pin gives every worker the same story's `file_scope`.
- **Worktree alone.** Each worker branch is cut from the delivery branch, which has every cohort brief in `xbrief/active/` (#4714 requires that). The worktree still has more than one eligible brief.
- **Move the other briefs out of `active/` on each worker branch.** Those moves ride into every PR and conflict at merge.

Current workaround: one headless `claude -p` process per story. Each process has its own environment, so its own pin. It works, but the workers are not visible or steerable from the parent session.

## Relation to open issues

- **#6185.** Its original body made this same claim and proposed `bindBranchToActiveStory` in the write hook. Its first comment withdrew the headline as not reproduced (a worker made four Edits to its own active brief, with two fencing briefs and no pin, and all were allowed). The issue was then retargeted to the launch-root lockout, and its arc kept `multiple-eligible` out of scope. This issue supplies the evaluator-level reproduction above and asks for that part to be decided on its own. I have not explained the four allowed Edits. Two candidates, both unverified: an exempt lifecycle-write path for the brief itself, or the outside-payload-root carve-out (#2885 / #3794) when the worktree is not under the payload root.
- **#5894.** Shows that a branch rename can sidestep branch-token binding, and that an environment pin has no provenance. A fix here must not add a new sidestep. That argues for the parent-written assignment record over the branch name as the binding source.
- **#5855, #4880, #4007.** Prior art for the binding, the recovery text and the fail-closed rule.

## Proposed direction (for design critique, not a bound design)

When there is no `boundPath`, let the write fence bind the write's worktree (`effectiveRoot`) to its story from the dispatch-written worker-auth assignment for that worktree. Then:

1. A write in worker A's worktree resolves to story A with no environment involved.
2. An environment pin that disagrees with the worktree record refuses. It does not silently win.
3. No record and more than one eligible brief stays fail-closed as today.
4. Grok Build stops depending on the spawn-time pin surviving into later writes.

## Open questions

1. Trust. The assignment registry is described as cooperative, not protection against a same-user process. Is that acceptable as write-fence authority, and how does it meet the #5894 binding contract?
2. Shell writes. Claude sub-agent shell commands start from the parent cwd. Does the fence cover recognized shell forms by target path, or only Write/Edit?
3. Destination. Claude `Agent` has no `cwd`. `isolation: "worktree"` lets the host create the worktree, which skips dest-place deposit reconstitution and the reservation mint. Is there a host hook that can hand worktree creation to `destPlaceImplementSpawn`? Not verified.
4. Occupancy. With one session identity for parent and sub-agents, does a per-worktree lease admit several workers of the same session family?
5. Adapter text. Until this is decided, should `host-claude-code.md` name headless per-story processes as the implement path for a multi-story cohort?

## Not in scope

- The launch-root lockout (#6185, #6206).
- Pin provenance and the other sidesteps (#5894).
- Host-side support for visible, steerable per-story worker sessions. That is a separate host request, tracked privately.
